summary: The team is focused on promoting Asia Start and Intelligent China programs while finalizing the Knowledge website redesign and resolving an email lockout, with ESG reporting and award applications also demanding attention.
summaryDetail: The top priority is driving promotion of China-based programs—Asia Start and Intelligent China—with the Berkeley program as a possible third, while US partnerships (Stanford, Columbia) are paused for Q1. This week, the team must resolve an Outlook account lockout by re-logging in on all devices and confirming backend access, and hold a 30-minute working session to mark feedback on the Knowledge website redesign, which will keep the current design with menu categorization changes and an editorial-style article display. Conversion tracking setup needs a brief and validation to support marketing analytics. Looking ahead, the ESG report draft is due next week, the AACSB 2027 Global Impact Award application requires Prof Zhu’s review before submission, and the Asia Start Beijing campus shoot needs a photographer brief.

decisions.text: Account lockout was caused by stale saved passwords repeatedly hitting the backend; fix by re-logging in on all devices.
Remove the standalone videos section; disperse videos by topic across the site
Keep the current Knowledge design largely as-is, with menu categorization as the main change
Bring BCI and BSI indices into the Knowledge section, similar to the school homepage banner
Do not add a stock-market ticker at the top of the homepage
Use the editorial-style layout as inspiration to display more articles, not to be followed exactly
Prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China programs for promotion, with Berkeley program as a potential third priority.
